hero.title: Julia & Suliaman
hero.subtitle: A bright celebration of the love we keep choosing.

emotionalAnchor: Our story started with a number I almost ignored, and it became the brightest thing in my life.

letter.opening: My Julia Helen Campbell, my love…
paragraphs: One whole year. I keep saying those two words out loud and they still feel too small for everything they carry. A year ago we had a date, a word called "worwor," and a three-hour wait I would gladly do again — and somehow that became my entire world.

Do you remember how we started? I remember every strange second of it. Your number appeared on my phone out of nowhere. To this day I cannot fully explain how — a cousin, work, some link I never really figured out. And at first, I ignored it. My only excuse is that I did not yet know that my light had just stepped into reach.

Then one night, that number spoke. And our very first real conversation was not romantic at all — it was an argument. In the middle of giving each other the worst of our energy, I called you ugly, and you gave it back to me with the exact same fire. I have never once regretted being so wrong in my life. You are the most beautiful person I know, in every way a person can be beautiful.

"Worwor." That word was an insult before it ever became a love story. But here is what I want you to remember about it: when that argument was over, neither of us walked away. We kept talking. Out of every way a story could begin, ours began with two people refusing to let a silly fight be the end of them.

Night after night we played question games on WhatsApp. Not the shallow kind — the kind where you hand a stranger your whole heart one answer at a time. You asked, I answered. I asked, you answered. Until I fell in love with your mind long before my eyes ever caught up, and I knew your name before I ever saw your face.

Then came the day we finally planned to meet in person. You were late, my love — three complete hours late. And for every single one of those hours, I stayed. People ask me why I never left. How do you explain that you already knew, before the first hello, that this was the person you would wait a lifetime for? Three hours was nothing. It still is nothing.

On the twenty-sixth of September, twenty-twenty-five, we made it official. That date stopped being just a date a long time ago. It is the day my whole life started making sense, and it is the day we will keep celebrating for as long as I am breathing.

Since that day I have watched you grow in ways that make my heart ache with gratitude. There is beauty in your patience, strength in your softness, and faith in the way you keep choosing love even when the world is loud.

And I love the names I have given you along the way. My chargie — the one who sits closest to my heart. Moama — my gift, my sanctuary, the person around whom I can finally breathe. Aunty — the warm comfort of being truly known. Big head — yes, still with love; your stubbornness and your fire are exactly what make you fierce for the people you love.

I have held your quiet tears and heard your loudest laughter, and both have taught me that love is not only romance. Love is mercy. Love is patience. Love is someone choosing you even on the days you cannot quite choose yourself.

And somewhere in all of it — between the number, the fight, the question games, and the three hours — you became Ly Nur. In Arabic, it means my light. Not because you glow when everything is arranged perfectly, but because you shine in the ordinary. In every quiet evening and every shared silence, you are the brightness that makes my life make sense.

We have grown through hard nights, small reconciliations, and gentle forgiveness. We are not perfect, and we were never trying to be. We are persistent. We are present. And we are living proof that even the crookedest beginning can become the straightest love.

So today, Julia Helen Campbell, I say thank you. Thank you for staying when the road felt uncertain. Thank you for choosing to move forward with me even on the days I made it hard. Thank you for being my friend, my love, my home.

I hope we keep growing into better versions of ourselves, individually and together. I hope our love becomes a refuge, a place of healing, a home. And I hope you never forget how deeply seen, how deeply valued, and how deeply held you are.

To me, you have never been invisible. Not for a single moment. You are treasured, loved, and irreplaceable. Happy first anniversary, my light. May the year ahead be gentler, truer, and more blessed than the last. I love you.
Yours, forever, from a number that became my everything — Suliaman.
prayers: I pray that our love stays rooted in grace, so that even when seasons change, we still choose kindness and forgiveness.
I pray God keeps guiding us toward honesty, humility, and hearts that make room for one another.
I pray that the number, the fight, the word "worwor," and the three-hour wait always remind us that what God joins together, we protect.
careerGoals: To step into places where your gifts are honored, your voice is heard, and your compassion becomes your strength.
To build a future where your work feels meaningful, sustainable, and aligned with the values that matter most to you.
To keep dreaming of work that allows you to care deeply without losing yourself, to lead with calm and confidence.
wishes: I wish we keep choosing each other long after the easy page turns — the way we did after that first argument.
I wish for a kind of peace in our home that feels like a soft prayer spoken aloud.
I wish every year ahead still feels like the three-hour wait — me standing right where I said I would be, and you always worth every minute of it.
